item.title: Mount Fuji UNESCO World Heritage Sites: The Sacred Mountain's Cultural Legacy — Guide
item.description: Mount Fuji was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2013 not as a natural wonder but as a cultural site, recognised as a ‘sacred place and source of artistic inspiration’ that has shaped Japanese religion, art and identity for centuries. The designation includes numerous component sites across the mountain’s northern foot in Yamanashi, from the Fujisan Hongu Sengen shrines that served as bases for pilgrim ascents, to the Fuji Five Lakes, Oshino Hakkai springs and other sacred natural features tied to Fuji worship, offering visitors a way to understand the mountain’s deep cultural significance beyond the view alone.

item.title: Iwate Power Spots: Sacred Mountains, Ancient Shrines & Spiritual Landscapes
item.description: Sacred Iwate: A Spiritual Journey Through Japan’s Northern Power Spots Iwate Prefecture, stretching from the rugged Sanriku coast to the sacred peaks of the Ōu Mountains, harbors some of northern Japan’s most profound spiritual sites. Far from the crowds of Kyoto and Kamakura, these power spots (reiki supotto) offer international visitors an intimate encounter with Japanese spirituality—where Buddhism, Shinto, and ancient animist beliefs interweave across a landscape that has channeled prayers for over a millennium.
